51482490.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to N-terminal His6-tagged USP8 catalytic domain (734 to 1110 residues) (unknown origin) expressed in Escherichia coli BL21 (DE3) cells by surface plasmon resonance method

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Deubiquitinating Enzyme Assay. The deubiquitinating activity was monitored via a Ubiquitin-rhodamine-110 fluorometric assay in assay buffer comprising 50 mM Tris–HCl, pH 7.5, 1 mM EDTA, 100 mM NaCl, and 0.05% (w/v) CHAPS. Briefly, compounds from an in-house compound library were diluted threefold from 100 μM and incubated with indicated deubiquitination enzymes (2 nM USP8, 6 nM USP2, or 5 nM USP7) for 30 min at room temperature in a 384-well plate. Ubiquitin-rhodamine (100 nM, Sigma SRP6139) substrates were added and incubated for 30 min. The whole reaction volume was 20 μL. The final fluorescence signals were acquired by an Envision multilabel reader using a 480 nm excitation/580 nm emission filter set. All data were analyzed in GraphPad Prism 5.0.
original_paragraph.SPR Analysis: An SPR-based binding assay was performed to determine the binding affinity between 13a and USP8. As shown in Figure 2D, the results revealed a potent and dose-dependent interaction between USP8 and 13a with a Kd value of 43.6 μM, which has the potential to be selected for further structure optimization. The initial docking screen was employed to generate the putative binding mode between USP8-CD and 13a (Figure 2E). The flavonoid skeleton formed a hydrophobic interaction with Leu977. In addition, O5- and O7-hydroxyls, respectively, formed hydrogen bonds with Asn980 and Arg982.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: Figure 2. Discovery and activity verification of leading compound 13a. (A) Flowchart of hierarchical high throughput screening for USP8 inhibitors. (B) Chemical structure of 13a. (C) Inhibitory activity of 13a determined in a Ubiquitin-Rho-110 fluorometric assay. (D) SPR-based binding assay of 13a with USP8-CD. (E) Putative binding mode between 13a and USP8-CD (PDB ID: 2GFO).
original_paragraph.Figure 2D description: Figure 2D shows the SPR-based binding assay of 13a with USP8-CD. The sensorgrams display response units (Ru) over time (s) for various concentrations of 13a: 100 μM, 76.9 μM, 59.2 μM, 45.3 μM, 35.0 μM, 26.9 μM, 20.7 μM, 15.9 μM, 12.3 μM, and 9.4 μM. The right panel shows the equilibrium binding curve with response units (Ru) versus 13a concentration (μM), yielding a Kd value of 43.6 μM.
original_paragraph.Table 1: Table 1. USP8 Inhibitory Activities of the Synthesized Compounds and the Control Compound HBX90659. Entry 1: Compound 13a, IC50 = 31.6 μM.
